title: Presigned URLs, Block Public Access and the bucket that leaked

videos.script: Everything in Quitanda's buckets is private. This lesson is about keeping it that way, and about the few ways it stops being true. {{private}} First, the presigned URL. It hands one person one file, with no account, until it expires. You will see that the URL carries the permission itself, and that moto never checks the expiry. {{url}} Then a real denial. moto has a mode that evaluates identity policies, and in it a dashboard user can read the reports and is refused when it tries to write one. {{deny}} Then the switches that stop a bucket from ever becoming public. moto stores them and enforces none, and you will watch a request with no credentials read a file anyway. {{switches}} And finally the bucket that leaked. The exposures that made the news were nearly always a line somebody wrote: a policy, an access list, or a link that lived too long. {{leak}} You will learn how each one happened, how to prevent it, and how to check from outside, with one request and no keys. {{check}}
